subject: Accountability summary and remediation tracker – April 16 service fallback
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Wu <emily.wu@ledgerly.com>, Ledgerly Ops <ops@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Accountability summary and remediation tracker – April 16 service fallback

Hi Emily / Ledgerly Ops team,

Thanks again for your patience while we finished our internal review of the April 16th fallback that impacted generation requests for a subset of Ledgerly accounts. Attached is a concise accountability summary plus a remediation tracker with owners and target dates. I wanted to call out the key points up front so you have a clear, actionable view: 

Summary (short):
- What happened: During a high-concurrency window at 18:04 UTC on Apr 16, a regression in request routing combined with a degraded cache eviction path caused persistent request queuing and a subset of requests to fall back to the lower-throughput CPU tier for ~22 minutes.
- Impact: Elevated latency and intermittent failures for ~12% of tokens for affected customers, including Ledgerly (you saw increased generation latency and a small fraction of timeouts).
- Root cause (short): A config change in the autoscaler wiring created an incorrect affinity for a new GPU pool; when combined with an aggressive prefix cache eviction, some live KV caches were evicted and could not be repopulated quickly.

Timeline (high level):
- 18:03 UTC Apr 16: Canary alert triggered for elevated queuing on gpu-pool-b
- 18:04–18:26 UTC Apr 16: Traffic routed to fallback CPU tier for a subset of requests
- 18:26 UTC Apr 16: Autoscaler rollback and manual cache warmup started
- 19:05 UTC Apr 16: Normal routing restored; error rates returned to baseline by 19:12 UTC

Immediate mitigations completed:
- Reverted autoscaler wiring change (owner: infra-team; completed Apr 16 18:26 UTC)
- Manual warmup of prefix KV caches for impacted pools (owner: runtime-ops; completed Apr 16 19:02 UTC)
- Safety rule added to prevent autoscaler changes from taking effect without staged canary runs (owner: platform-safety; applied Apr 17)

Committed follow-ups (owners & ETA):
1) Robust canary gating for autoscaler config pushes — Marissa Cole — ETA: 2027-04-28
2) Prefix cache resilience improvements (prevent eviction storms) — Hannah Schmitt — ETA: 2027-05-12
3) Fallback path performance hardening (reduce CPU-tier tail latency) — Runtime team — ETA: 2027-05-05
4) Customer-facing post-incident doc and remediation tracker (this file + spreadsheet) — Alex Martinez — ETA: 2027-04-20 (attached)

Requested next steps from Ledgerly:
- Confirm whether you want a short credit applied for April 16 (we propose a single-day service credit equivalent to 10% of billable inference for impacted calls).
- Confirm timing for a 30-minute follow-up sync next week to walk the remediation tracker (we can do Tue/Wed).

Attachments: accountability_summary_ledgerly_20270418.pdf (RCA summary + timeline), repro-logs-apr16.zip (redacted logs), remediation-tracker-20270418.xlsx

If you prefer, we can also schedule a short incident walkthrough with engineering leads and your SREs. I appreciate your partnership on this.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Credit calc: We propose a 10% one-day credit for billable inference volume during the impacted window. Calculation basis: Ledgerly billable token count for Apr 16 (00:00–23:59 UTC) * 10%. We can supply the token counts and math in a spreadsheet.
- One-page timeline: I have a distilled timeline in the accountability_summary_ledgerly_20270418.pdf; suggest we create a Ledgerly-branded one-pager and publish to their stakeholder portal after their review.

Please confirm the owners/ETAs below so I can reply to Emily and confirm the Tue 14:00 EDT slot.
- Checksum & redacted logs to compliance — Alex — by 2027-04-20 23:59 UTC
- Credit calculation and spreadsheet — Marissa — by 2027-04-20 17:00 UTC
- Branded one-page timeline — Hannah — draft by 2027-04-21

Also: do we want to escalate this to customer success for any renewal implications? My read is yes, flag to CS but do not pull in yet until Ledgerly confirms credit ask.

Thanks,
Alex

3) One-page timeline for stakeholders- Draft a Ledgerly-branded one-pager summarizing the event and the fixes. Owner: Hannah Schmitt — draft by 2027-04-21; final after Ledgerly review.

We will send the redacted logs and the credit spreadsheet to you by EOD today. If you want the one-pager earlier, Hannah can prioritize an initial draft before the call.

Apologies again for the disruption — we take these incidents seriously and are committed to preventing recurrence. I’ll be on the sync and available for any questions.
